response.text:
Recent work supports separating product function, compatibility, and subjective preference. TREC’s recommendation task distinguishes substitutes from complements by function; ECCR (2024) additionally requires complementary recommendations to be compatible and relevant. Practical adaptation: compare actual catalog candidates with similar textual relevance but different functional relationships; flag compatibility conflicts only when titles/descriptions explicitly establish incompatible models, connectors, dimensions, or formats. Co-purchase alone cannot establish complementarity, and a substitute is not automatically redundant. [TREC task](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html), [ECCR](https://www.amazon.science/publications/eccr-explainable-and-coherent-complement-recommendation-based-on-large-language-models).

Hard negatives need uncertainty handling. Hard-BPR (2024) and CNSDiff (2025) identify false negatives as a risk: unobserved items can be relevant, while exposure/popularity confounding can make difficult negatives misleading. Suggested diagnostic: match candidates by training-frequency bucket and title/description similarity, then vary one evidenced attribute. For media, probe explicitly documented language, format, creator, or series distinctions against repeated historical patterns, treating those patterns as tentative preference evidence. FineRec (2024) extracts attribute–opinion pairs from reviews; that supervision is unavailable here, so its preference claims cannot be reproduced from titles alone. [Hard-BPR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276), [CNSDiff](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07243), [FineRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12975).

These are proposed adaptations, not validated labels: retain supporting text spans, use only preceding training history, and return unknown when evidence is missing or contradictory. Report supported-pair ranking rates, score margins, support counts, and unknown coverage by category. Keep these probes auxiliary; select models using the unchanged macro validation HR@10.
